Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test "testCircleFitting" tests the LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer behavior on fitting circles and checks RMS and parameter errors. The current bug report points out an inconsistency in the AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer between handling residual weights in getRMS() and getChiSquare(). Specifically, residualsWeights are treated multiplicatively in getRMS() (summing residual² * weight) which is the standard way to apply weights affecting the variance of residuals. However, in getChiSquare(), weights are applied as denominators (summing residual² / weight), which contradicts standard weighting where weights should multiply the residual squared in both cases.

Inspection of the code snippets from AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer shows:
- getRMS() computes the root mean square error as sqrt( sum(residual² * weight) / rows )
- getChiSquare() computes chi-square as sum(residual² / weight)

The residualsWeights array is meant to represent observation weights. The inconsistency means getChiSquare calculation is wrong if these are weights because dividing by weights instead of multiplying is incorrect, leading to inconsistent diagnostics and statistics, which might be impacting the optimization results reliability tested in testCircleFitting.

This discrepancy is the likely root cause of the test failure or related inaccurate error estimation seen in the circle fitting test. Correcting getChiSquare() to multiply by residualsWeights instead of dividing would align the behavior with getRMS() and statistical conventions.

Recent bug reports referencing LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer and weighting issues support this hypothesis. No other relevant code snippets from LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer were found, indicating the root cause lies in AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer's statistical computation methods.

Hence, the key bug is the incorrect use of weights as denominators in getChiSquare(), inconsistent with getRMS() and standard weighted least squares formulations.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
